title: Module review
subtitle: Everything from Sweet Wine
objectives: Explain how sweet wines keep their sugar

steps.prompt: Match each method to a wine.
steps.explanation: Each method concentrates sugar in a different way.

steps.prompt: What stops grey rot from developing instead of noble rot?
steps.explanation: Dry afternoons stop the fungus from turning destructive.
Not true. It is made from dried grapes but fermented nearly dry. Recioto is its sweet sibling.

steps.prompt: Which grapes are known for great sweet wines thanks to high acidity?
steps.explanation: Gewürztraminer can make sweet wines, but its naturally low acidity is a weakness, not a strength.

steps.prompt: Ice wine grapes must freeze naturally at minus ____ degrees Celsius or colder.
steps.explanation: Minus 7 degrees is the common legal threshold in Canada and Germany.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Sweet wines stop fermentation early or start with concentrated grapes
Noble rot, late harvest, freezing and drying concentrate sugar
High acidity keeps great sweet wines fresh
Amarone shows that dried grapes can also make dry wine
